panels.rationale: Single coherent PET-CT study of patient 2 (one figure, no panel letters → panel A). The article contrasts IgM multiple myeloma with Waldenström macroglobulinemia in two case reports; the in-text description bound to Fig. 4 reports multiple enlarged perihepatic/peripancreatic/mesenteric lymph nodes and splenomegaly with normal liver tests — a systemic lymphoplasmacytic pattern that fits Waldenström macroglobulinemia rather than IgM myeloma (prior caption triage likewise assigns patient 2 to Waldenström). The coronal PET and fused axial PET-CT visibly demonstrate FDG-avid abdominal/mesenteric lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly, mapped to the provided vocabulary. No skin, ethnicity, or age is stated. Confidence is high for the findings and imaging, slightly tempered because the caption itself does not name the disease (attribution rests on the case context and the characteristic manifestation pattern).

A: Real patient inguinal lymph node core-biopsy immunohistochemistry from the Waldenström macroglobulinemia case (disease-focused article title); caption states CD10 is positive in the lymphoma cells (strong brown stain). A: H&E bone marrow panel from a disease-focused lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenström macroglobulinemia article; the caption states increased lymphoid cells, supporting a classic lymphoplasmacytic marrow infiltrate. No panel letter is printed, so panels are labeled positionally. B: IgM immunohistochemistry of the same patient marrow shows strong brown IgM positivity, supporting a B-cell lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate in the Waldenström macroglobulinemia/lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma case. C: CD20 immunohistochemistry shows strong B-cell positivity in the marrow infiltrate; combined with the disease-focused article title and caption, this supports Waldenström macroglobulinemia/lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma. D: CD3 immunohistochemistry is reported as negative for the marrow lymphoid infiltrate, supporting B-cell rather than T-cell disease in this lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma/Waldenström macroglobulinemia case.

in_text_mentions: Pathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of LPL (Fig. 2). The patient then underwent a bone marrow biopsy and a computed tomography (CT) scan of the entire chest, abdomen, and pelvis. No abnormalities were found. According to the Ann Arbor–Cotswald staging system for lymphomas, this case of CPA LPL was classified as Stage I, indicating that the cancer was located in a single region.

in_text_mentions: We present a 78‐year‐old male with a history of WM diagnosed in 2014 when a bone marrow biopsy showed LPL (Figure 2A,B), which harbored the MYD88 p.L265P mutation. He underwent six cycles of bendamustine/rituximab and achieved complete remission. In 2019, he returned with a rising IgM level (859 mg/dl) in the setting of multiple new 3–4 cm subcutaneous nodules on his lower extremities (Figure 1A).
